steps.question: Do the 12 kidney samples in counts.csv match metadata.csv, is the two-batch design genuinely balanced across treated (n=6) and control (n=6), and how much variance does batch explain relative to condition?

steps.description: Load counts.csv and metadata.csv, align sample columns to metadata rows (fail loudly on any mismatch or ordering difference rather than silently reindexing), cross-tabulate condition x batch and report the table, drop genes with near-zero counts using a filter suited to n=6 per group (e.g. keep genes with count >= 10 in at least 6 samples), construct a DESeqDataSet with design ~ batch + condition and control as the reference level, then compute VST and produce: PCA coloured by condition and separately by batch with percent-variance on the axes, a sample-sample Euclidean distance heatmap annotated by both factors, library-size / total-count per sample, and a variance-partition-style summary of how much of the top-variable-gene variance tracks batch versus condition. caveats: With 6 vs 6, genes with low counts have unstable dispersion estimates — the shrunken LFC is the one to interpret

Cook's-distance outlier filtering can silently drop genes at this sample size — report how many were flagged
steps.context: This is the step that answers the research question. The design is balanced across two batches, so batch enters the negative-binomial GLM as an additive covariate (~ batch + condition) and the condition coefficient is the treated-vs-control effect adjusted for batch. n=6 per group is a modest but workable sample size for DESeq2; the result must be reported with its actual power limits rather than as a definitive catalogue.
steps.question: Which of the ~12,000 kidney genes differ between treated (n=6) and control (n=6) after adjusting for the two processing batches?
constraints: Fit the model on raw counts with design ~ batch + condition — never on a ComBat-corrected or otherwise batch-adjusted matrix
Use apeglm for LFC shrinkage on the coefficient (not the deprecated normal shrinkage); report both shrunken and unshrunken values
Do not filter genes by fold change before FDR correction; apply BH across all tested genes
Report independent-filtering behaviour (how many genes have padj = NA and why)
steps.description: Run DESeq() on the filtered object from T1S1 with design ~ batch + condition and extract the condition treated_vs_control contrast. Report: base mean, unshrunken log2FC with SE, apeglm-shrunken log2FC, Wald p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value for every tested gene, written as a complete results table sorted by adjusted p-value. As robustness checks on the modelling choice, refit (a) the naive ~ condition model without the batch term and (b) limma-voom with ~ batch + condition, and report the overlap of the significant sets among the three fits together with the rank correlation of their log2FCs. Also report the batch coefficient's own significance so the size of the nuisance effect is on record. Write a plain-language summary naming the top up- and down-regulated genes with their effect sizes.

The number of genes with padj < 0.05, with padj < 0.10, and with padj < 0.05 & |log2FC| > 1 are each reported explicitly
Volcano plot, MA plot and a top-gene heatmap annotated by condition and batch are produced

Overlap between the ~ batch + condition DESeq2 result, the ~ condition-only result, and the limma-voom result is quantified (counts and log2FC rank correlation), with any material disagreement discussed
The direction convention is stated: positive log2FC means higher in treated relative to control
The report states the n=6 vs n=6 power limitation and does not present the significant list as exhaustive

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of the treated-vs-control signature
caveats: Hallmark and GO overlap heavily in membership; correlated significant sets are not independent findings
A significant NES with a small leading edge driven by two or three genes is weak evidence — report leading-edge size
Kidney tissue signatures can be dominated by a few highly expressed structural genes; check that top sets are not driven by them alone
steps.context: Takes the full ranked gene list from T1S2 (all tested genes ranked by shrunken log2FC, or by the signed Wald statistic) rather than a thresholded list, because at n=6 per group the padj<0.05 set may be too small for a reliable over-representation test. The dataset is Homo sapiens and the counts are keyed by HGNC gene symbol, matching the symbol-based human gene set collections available in the reference store — no identifier conversion is required. Reference data needed: human hallmark gene sets and human GO biological-process gene sets, both as symbol-keyed gene set collections; resolve them from the environment's reference store at run time rather than assuming a path.
steps.question: Which biological processes and hallmark states are coordinately shifted between treated and control kidney samples, beyond the individual gene calls?
constraints: Use the human (Homo sapiens) symbol-keyed gene set collections — never the mouse or rat collections
Rank on the full tested gene list from T1S2; do not pre-filter to significant genes for the GSEA arm
Use the tested-gene universe from T1S2 as background for the over-representation arm, not the whole genome
Set a fixed random seed so the permutation-based p-values are reproducible
steps.description: Run pre-ranked GSEA (fgsea) on the complete treated-vs-control ranking from T1S2 against the human hallmark collection and the human GO biological-process collection, restricting to gene sets with 15-500 members present in the tested universe. Report normalised enrichment score, nominal p, BH-adjusted p and leading-edge genes per set; produce a dot/bar plot of the top enriched sets by NES in each direction and enrichment curves for the few strongest. Because GO-BP is a nested hierarchy, collapse redundant parent/child hits before reporting a headline count. As a secondary readout, run an over-representation test on the padj<0.05 gene set against the same collections using the tested genes as background, and note where the two approaches agree. If either gene set collection is not present in the environment at run time, report that explicitly and proceed with whichever is available — the differential expression answer from T1S2 stands independently of this step.
acceptance_criteria: GSEA results tables for the human hallmark and human GO-BP collections are written with NES, pval, padj and leading-edge genes per set
The gene universe used (tested genes from T1S2) and the min/max set size filters are stated
Redundant GO-BP parent/child hits are collapsed before a headline count is reported
Plots of the top enriched sets in both directions are produced
Any gene set collection that could not be resolved from the reference store is named explicitly rather than silently skipped
Enriched sets are interpreted as coordinate shifts, not as evidence of mechanism

plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch covariate
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single bulk RNA-seq experiment: /data/inputs/counts/counts.csv holds raw integer salmon gene-level counts for 12,000 gene symbols x 12 samples, and /data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv gives condition (treated, n=6; control, n=6) and batch (two processing batches) for each of the 12 samples. The stated design is balanced — each batch holds both conditions — so batch is a nuisance factor that is not confounded with treatment and can be handled directly as a covariate in the model rather than by removing it from the data. That drives the plan.

T1S1 builds the DESeq2 object from the two CSVs, verifies sample-name concordance between counts columns and metadata rows, confirms the condition x batch cross-tabulation is genuinely balanced (a 6/6 split with both conditions in each batch), applies a low-count filter appropriate to n=6 per group, and produces VST-based QC: PCA coloured by condition and by batch, sample-sample distance heatmap, and library-size summaries. This step decides empirically how much variance batch actually explains — the design says it is balanced, but the profile cannot say whether the batch effect is large, negligible, or accompanied by an outlier sample.

T1S2 runs the actual contrast, treated vs control, with ~ batch + condition on raw counts. Modelling batch as a covariate is the correct treatment for a balanced two-batch design: it absorbs batch variance while leaving the condition estimate unbiased, and it preserves the raw-count likelihood that DESeq2 needs. Batch-corrected matrices (ComBat/removeBatchEffect) are used for visualisation only, never as input to the count model, because they distort the dispersion estimates and inflate significance. The step reports shrunken log2 fold changes (apeglm) alongside unshrunken ones, BH-adjusted p-values, and — as a robustness check on the modelling choice — an interaction-free comparison against the naive ~ condition model plus a limma-voom ~ batch + condition fit, so the gene list is not an artefact of one estimator. With 6 vs 6 and 12,000 genes the study is modestly powered; the step must state the effective power plainly rather than lean on a nominal FDR cut.

T2S1 takes the ranked gene list forward to pathway level using the human hallmark and GO-BP collections staged in the reference store (organism matches: Homo sapiens, HGNC symbols, and the counts already carry gene symbols as row identifiers, so no ID mapping is needed). GSEA on the full shrunken-LFC ranking is preferred over an over-representation test on a thresholded list, because at n=6 per group the significant-gene set may be small and thresholding throws away the ranking information. This step enriches the interpretation; if the gene sets are absent at run time it reports that and the DE result from T1S2 still answers the research question.
